metadata.title: A New Proof of Szemerédi's Theorem for Arithmetic Progressions of Length Four
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json registry lists this paper as 'Lower Bounds of Tower Type for Szemeredi's Uniformity Lemma' (Gowers 1997), but the source PDF/text is actually 'A New Proof of Szemerédi's Theorem for Arithmetic Progressions of Length Four' (Gowers, GAFA Vol. 8, 1998, pp. 529–551). Extraction follows the PDF content.

nodes.name: Szemerédi's Theorem
nodes.statement: For any positive integer $k$ and any real number $\delta > 0$, there exists $N$ such that every subset of $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$ of cardinality at least $\delta N$ contains an arithmetic progression of length $k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Every set of integers of positive density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
conclusions: There exists $N$ such that every $A \subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $|A| \ge \delta N$ contains a $k$-term arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Discrete Fourier Coefficient on $\mathbb{Z}_N$
nodes.statement: For $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{C}$, the $r$-th Fourier coefficient is $\tilde f(r) = \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_N} f(s) \omega^{-rs}$, where $\omega = \exp(2\pi i / N)$.

nodes.name: Convolution $f \ast g$
nodes.statement: For $f, g : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{C}$, define $(f \ast g)(s) = \sum_{t-u=s} f(t) g(u)$. This convention departs from the standard convolution.

nodes.name: Balanced Function $f_A$ of a Set $A$
nodes.statement: For $A \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ of size $\delta N$, the balanced function is $f_A(s) = 1-\delta$ if $s \in A$ and $f_A(s) = -\delta$ if $s \notin A$. Equivalently, $f_A$ is the characteristic function minus the constant $\delta$.

nodes.name: $\alpha$-Uniform Function and Set
nodes.statement: $f$ is $\alpha$-uniform if $\sum_r |\tilde f(r)|^4 \le \alpha N^4$. A set $A$ is $\alpha$-uniform if its balanced function is.
nodes.notes: Coincides with the Chung–Graham notion of a quasirandom subset of $\mathbb{Z}_N$.

nodes.name: Difference Operator $\Delta(f;k)$
nodes.statement: For $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ (or $\mathbb{C}$) and $k \in \mathbb{Z}_N$, $\Delta(f;k)(s) = f(s)\overline{f(s-k)}$. If $f(s) = \omega^{\phi(s)}$, then $\Delta(f;k)(s) = \omega^{\phi(s) - \phi(s-k)}$.

nodes.name: Quadratically $\alpha$-Uniform Function and Set
nodes.statement: $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{D}$ is quadratically $\alpha$-uniform if $\sum_u \sum_v |\sum_s f(s) \overline{f(s-u)} \overline{f(s-v)} f(s-u-v)|^2 \le \alpha N^4$. A set is quadratically $\alpha$-uniform if its balanced function is.

nodes.name: Squares and Cubes in $\mathbb{Z}_N$
nodes.statement: A square is a sequence $(s, s+a, s+b, s+a+b)$. A cube is $(s, s+a, s+b, s+c, s+a+b, s+a+c, s+b+c, s+a+b+c)$.

nodes.name: Additive Quadruple
nodes.statement: Given $\phi : B \to \mathbb{Z}_N$, a quadruple $(a,b,c,d) \in B^4$ is additive if $a+b = c+d$ and $\phi(a)+\phi(b) = \phi(c)+\phi(d)$.

nodes.name: $d$-dimensional Arithmetic Progression
nodes.statement: A set of the form $P_1 + \cdots + P_d$, where each $P_i$ is an ordinary arithmetic progression. It is proper if every $x \in Q$ has a unique representation $x_1 + \cdots + x_d$ with $x_i \in P_i$.

nodes.name: Equivalent Characterizations of $\alpha$-Uniformity
nodes.statement: For $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{D}$, the following are equivalent (up to polynomial relations among the constants $c_i$): (i) $\sum_r |\tilde f(r)|^4 \le c_1 N^4$; (ii) $\max_r |\tilde f(r)| \le c_2 N$; (iii) $\sum_k |\sum_s f(s)\overline{f(s-k)}|^2 \le c_3 N^3$; (iv) $\sum_k |\sum_s f(s)\overline{g(s-k)}|^2 \le c_4 N^2 \|g\|_2^2$ for every $g : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{C}$.
conclusions: (i)–(iv) are equivalent characterizations of $\alpha$-uniformity.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Use Fourier identities (1) and (2) plus Cauchy–Schwarz to relate the four quantities.

nodes.name: Equivalent Characterizations of Quadratic $\alpha$-Uniformity
nodes.statement: For $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{D}$, the following are equivalent: (i) $\sum_u \sum_v |\sum_s f(s)\overline{f(s-u)f(s-v)}f(s-u-v)|^2 \le c_1 N^4$; (ii) $\sum_k \sum_r |\Delta(f;k)^\sim(r)|^4 \le c_2 N^5$; (iii) $|\Delta(f;k)^\sim(r)| \ge c_3 N$ for at most $c_3^2 N$ pairs $(k,r)$; (iv) $\Delta(f;k)$ is $c_4$-uniform for all but $c_4 N$ values of $k$.
conclusions: (i)–(iv) are equivalent characterizations of quadratic $\alpha$-uniformity.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Equivalence of (i)–(ii) by expansion and applying Lemma 1 to each $\Delta(f;k)$. Implications (ii)↔(iii)↔(iv) by elementary counting.

nodes.name: Sum of $\alpha$-Uniform Functions
nodes.statement: If $f_i : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{D}$ is $\alpha_i$-uniform for $1 \le i \le k$, then $f_1 + \cdots + f_k$ is $(\alpha_1^{1/4} + \cdots + \alpha_k^{1/4})^4$-uniform.
conclusions: $f_1 + \cdots + f_k$ is $(\sum \alpha_i^{1/4})^4$-uniform.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Immediate from the fact that $f \mapsto (\sum_r |\tilde f(r)|^4)^{1/4}$ is a norm.

nodes.name: Translates of a Quadratically Uniform Set
nodes.statement: Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ be quadratically $\alpha$-uniform of size $\delta N$. Then for all but $\alpha^{1/2} N$ values of $k$, $A \cap (A+k)$ is $81 \alpha^{1/2}$-uniform; and for all but $\alpha^{1/4} N$ values of $k$, $||A \cap (A+k)| - \delta^2 N| \le \alpha^{1/8} N$.
conclusions: $A \cap (A+k)$ is $81\alpha^{1/2}$-uniform for all but $\alpha^{1/2} N$ values of $k$.
$||A \cap (A+k)| - \delta^2 N| \le \alpha^{1/8} N$ for all but $\alpha^{1/4} N$ values of $k$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Decompose $A \cap (A+k)(s) = \delta^2 + \delta f(s) + \delta f(s-k) + f(s)f(s-k)$ and apply Lemmas 1–3.

nodes.name: Tchebyshev-type Concentration Bound
nodes.statement: Let $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{R}^+$ with $\|f\|_1 = wN$ and $\|f\|_2^2 \le (1+\epsilon) w^2 N$. For any $A \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$, $|\sum_{s \in A} f(s) - w|A|| \le \epsilon^{1/2} w N^{1/2} |A|^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz to $\sum_{s\in A}|f(s) - w| \le |A|^{1/2}(\sum_{s\in A}(f(s)-w)^2)^{1/2}$ and use the variance bound.

nodes.name: Counting 3-APs via Uniformity
nodes.statement: If $A, B, C \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ have sizes $\alpha N, \beta N, \gamma N$ and $C$ is $\eta$-uniform, then $|\sum_r |A \cap (B+r) \cap (C+2r)| - \alpha\beta\gamma N^2| \le \eta N^2$.
conclusions: $|\sum_r |A \cap (B+r) \cap (C+2r)| - \alpha\beta\gamma N^2| \le \eta N^2$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Expand using Fourier coefficients: $\sum_r |A \cap (B+r) \cap (C+2r)| = N^{-1}(\sum_{p\ne 0} \tilde A(p)\tilde B(-2p)\tilde C(p)) + N^{-1}|A||B||C|$, then apply Cauchy–Schwarz with the $\eta$-uniformity of $C$.

nodes.name: Counting 4-APs via Quadratic Uniformity
nodes.statement: If $A, B, C, D \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ have sizes $\alpha N, \beta N, \gamma N, \delta N$ with $C$ being $\eta$-uniform and $D$ being quadratically $\eta$-uniform for $\eta \le 2^{-20}$, then $|\sum_r |A\cap(B+r)\cap(C+2r)\cap(D+3r)| - \alpha\beta\gamma\delta N^2| \le 3\eta^{1/16} N^2 / (\beta\gamma\delta)$.
assumptions: $A, B, C, D \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ with sizes $\alpha N, \beta N, \gamma N, \delta N$
conclusions: $|\sum_r |A\cap(B+r)\cap(C+2r)\cap(D+3r)| - \alpha\beta\gamma\delta N^2| \le 3\eta^{1/16} N^2/(\beta\gamma\delta)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Set $f(s) = \sum_r B(s-r)C(s-2r)D(s-3r)$ and bound $\|f\|_1$, $\|f\|_2$ via Lemma 6 and quadratic uniformity of $C, D$, then apply Lemma 5.

nodes.name: Bound $\|f\|_1$ via Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Using $D$ being $\eta^{1/2}$-uniform (from Lemma 4) and Lemma 6, $N^2(\beta\gamma\delta - \eta^{1/2}) \le \|f\|_1 \le N^2(\beta\gamma\delta + \eta^{1/2})$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|f\|_2^2$ via substitution and Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Substitute $p = q-r$ to rewrite $\|f\|_2^2$, then bound terms using Lemma 4 (translates of $C, D$ small except for few $p$).

nodes.name: Conclude via Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5 with $\epsilon = 4\eta^{1/8}/(\beta^2\gamma^2\delta^2)$ to deduce $|\sum_{s\in A} f(s) - \alpha\beta\gamma\delta N^2| \le 3\eta^{1/16} N^2/(\beta\gamma\delta)$.

nodes.name: Quadratically Uniform Sets Contain 4-APs
nodes.statement: Let $A_0 \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ be quadratically $\eta$-uniform of size $\delta N$, where $\eta \le 2^{-208}\delta^{112}$ and $N > 200\delta^{-3}$. Then $A_0$ contains an arithmetic progression of length four.
conclusions: $A_0$ contains a 4-term arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 8
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 7 with $A = B = A_0 \cap [2N/5, 3N/5)$ and $C = D = A_0$. Get $\ge \delta^4 N^2/200$ sequences $(a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d)$; only $\delta N$ have $d=0$, so a genuine 4-AP exists with $d \ne 0$ that lifts to $\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Many Additive Quadruples from Large Fourier Coefficients of $\Delta(f;k)$
nodes.statement: Let $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{D}$, $B \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$, $\phi : B \to \mathbb{Z}_N$. If $\sum_{k\in B} |\Delta(f;k)^\sim(\phi(k))|^2 \ge \alpha N^3$, then there are at least $\alpha^4 N^3$ quadruples $(a,b,c,d) \in B^4$ with $a+b=c+d$ and $\phi(a)+\phi(b)=\phi(c)+\phi(d)$.
conclusions: At least $\alpha^4 N^3$ additive quadruples in $B^4$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 9
nodes.statement: Expand the Fourier sum, substitute $u = s-t$, apply Cauchy–Schwarz and Lemma 1(iv→i) to extract a Fourier coefficient inequality, then sum to count additive quadruples.

nodes.name: Expand and substitute $u = s-t$
nodes.statement: Expanding the assumption gives $\sum_{k\in B}\sum_{s,t} f(s)\overline{f(s-k)f(t)}f(t-k)\omega^{-\phi(k)(s-t)} \ge \alpha N^3$; substituting $u = s-t$ yields $\sum_k \sum_{s,u} f(s)\overline{f(s-k)f(s-u)}f(s-k-u)\omega^{-\phi(k)u} \ge \alpha N^3$.

nodes.name: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz
nodes.statement: Since $|f(s)| \le 1$, get $\sum_u \sum_s |\sum_{k\in B} f(s-k)\overline{f(s-k-u)}\omega^{-\phi(k)u}|^2 \ge \alpha^2 N^4$ via Cauchy–Schwarz.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1 (iv → i) and sum over $u$
nodes.statement: Using Lemma 1 and summing over $u$ gives $\sum_u \sum_r |\sum_{k\in B} \omega^{\phi(k)u - rk}|^4 \ge \alpha^4 N^5$, which expands as $N^2$ times the number of additive quadruples.

nodes.name: Freiman's Theorem
nodes.statement: For each constant $C$ there exist $d, K$ depending only on $C$ such that whenever $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ has $|A| = m$ and $|A+A| \le Cm$, there is a $d$-dimensional arithmetic progression $Q$ with $|Q| \le Km$ and $A \subset Q$.
conclusions: There is an arithmetic progression $Q$ of dimension $\le d$ with $|Q| \le Km$ and $A \subset Q$.

nodes.name: Combinatorial Lemma on Pairwise Intersections
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a set of size $m$, $\delta > 0$, and $A_1, \ldots, A_n \subset X$ with $\sum_{x,y} |A_x \cap A_y| \ge \delta^2 m n^2$. There is $K \subset [n]$ with $|K| \ge 2^{-1/2} \delta^5 n$ such that for at least 90% of $(x,y) \in K^2$, $|A_x \cap A_y| \ge \delta^2 m / 2$.
conclusions: There exists $K \subset [n]$ with $|K| \ge 2^{-1/2}\delta^5 n$ such that 90% of pairs $(x,y) \in K^2$ satisfy $|A_x \cap A_y| \ge \delta^2 m / 2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 11
nodes.statement: Probabilistic argument: pick five random $j_1, \ldots, j_5 \le m$ uniformly, set $X = E_{j_1} \cap \cdots \cap E_{j_5}$ where $E_j = B_j^2$, $B_j = \{i : j \in A_i\}$. Use Hölder to bound $E[|X|] \ge \delta^{10} n^2$ and $E[|Y|] \le \delta^{10} n^2 / 32$, yielding the claim.

nodes.name: Quantitative Balog–Szemerédi Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^D$ with $|A| = m$ and $\|A \ast A\|_2^2 \ge c_0 m^3$. There exist constants $c, C$ depending only on $c_0$ and a subset $A'' \subset A$ with $|A''| \ge cm$ such that $|A'' - A''| \le Cm$.
conclusions: There exists $A'' \subset A$ with $|A''| \ge cm$ and $|A'' - A''| \le Cm$, where $c, C$ depend only on $c_0$.
nodes.notes: Refines Balog–Szemerédi [BSz 1994] with explicit polynomial bounds, avoiding Szemerédi's regularity lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 12
nodes.statement: Define popular differences and a graph $G$ on $A$ joined by popular differences; refine via Lemma 11 to get a subset with most pairwise neighbourhood intersections large; deduce $|A'' - A''| \lesssim m$ by counting representations of differences.

nodes.name: Identify popular differences
nodes.statement: $f(x) = A \ast A(x)$ satisfies $\|f\|_\infty \le m$, $\|f\|_2^2 \ge c_0 m^3$, $\|f\|_1 = m^2$; hence $f(x) \ge c_0 m / 2$ for at least $c_0 m / 2$ values of $x$ (popular differences).

nodes.name: Build graph $G$ and find high-degree vertices
nodes.statement: Define $G$ on $A$ by joining $a \sim b$ when $b-a$ is popular. Average degree $\ge c_0^2 m / 4$, so $\ge c_0^2 m / 8$ vertices have degree $\ge c_0^2 m / 8$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 11 to neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: Lemma 11 gives $A' \subset \{a_1, \ldots, a_n\}$ of size $\ge \delta^5 n / \sqrt{2}$ with most pairs $A_i \cap A_j$ of size $\ge \delta^2 m / 2$.

nodes.name: Count representations of differences in $A''$
nodes.statement: Refine to $A''$ with high degree in $H$; use that for $a_i, a_j \in A''$ at least $(3/5)|A'|$ shared neighbours produce many representations of $a_i - a_j$ as $(p-q)-(r-s)-((t-u)-(v-w))$ with $p,\ldots,w \in A$, bounding $|A'' - A''|$.

nodes.name: Freiman-type Conclusion via Balog–Szemerédi
nodes.statement: Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^D$ with $|A| = m$ and $\|A \ast A\|_2^2 \ge c_0 m^3$. There is an arithmetic progression $Q$ of cardinality $\le Cm$ and dimension $\le d$ with $|A \cap Q| \ge cm$, where $C, d, c$ depend only on $c_0$.
conclusions: There is a $d$-dim arithmetic progression $Q$ with $|Q| \le Cm$ and $|A \cap Q| \ge cm$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 13
nodes.statement: Combine Theorem 10 (Freiman) with Proposition 12 (Balog–Szemerédi refinement).

nodes.name: Linear Structure on Functions with Many Additive Quadruples
nodes.statement: Let $B \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ with $|B| = \beta N$ and $\phi : B \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ have at least $c_0 N^3$ additive quadruples. Then there exist $\gamma, \eta$ depending on $\beta, c_0$, a mod-$N$ arithmetic progression $P \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ with $|P| \ge N\gamma$, and a linear $\psi : P \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ such that $\phi(s) = \psi(s)$ for at least $\eta |P|$ values of $s \in P$.
conclusions: There exist a mod-$N$ AP $P$ with $|P| \ge N\gamma$ and linear $\psi : P \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ with $\phi(s) = \psi(s)$ for $\ge \eta |P|$ values of $s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 14
nodes.statement: View graph $\Gamma$ of $\phi$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$; apply Corollary 13 (with Ruzsa modification giving proper $Q$) to obtain proper $Q = P_1 + \cdots + P_d$ with $|\Gamma \cap Q| \ge cN$; partition $Q$ into 1D APs of size $\ge (cN)^{1/d}$; pass to a non-vertical AP to extract a linear function.

nodes.name: Quadratic Bias from Large $\Delta(f;k)$ Coefficients
nodes.statement: Let $A \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ have balanced function $f$, and $P$ a mod-$N$ arithmetic progression of cardinality $T$. If there exist $\lambda, \mu$ with $\sum_{k \in P} |\Delta(f;k)^\sim(\lambda k + \mu)|^2 \ge \beta N^2 T$, then there exist quadratic polynomials $\psi_0, \ldots, \psi_{N-1}$ with $\sum_s |\sum_{z \in P+s} f(z) \omega^{-\psi_s(z)}| \ge \beta N T / \sqrt{2}$.
conclusions: There exist quadratic polynomials $\psi_s$ with $\sum_s |\sum_{z \in P+s} f(z)\omega^{-\psi_s(z)}| \ge \beta N T / \sqrt 2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 15
nodes.statement: Expand assumption, substitute $u = s-t$ and parametrize $P = \{x+id : 1 \le i \le T\}$; introduce auxiliary $\gamma(s,y)$ and reduce to a general bilinear lemma yielding a quadratic polynomial via Cauchy–Schwarz on $g_1, g_2, g_3$.

nodes.name: Reparametrize $P$ and define $\gamma(s,y)$
nodes.statement: Set $P = \{x+d, x+2d, \ldots, x+td\}$, rewrite the inequality, define $\gamma(s,y)$ via $\sum_{i,j} f(s-x-id) \overline{f(s-y-jd)} f(s-x-id-y-jd) \omega^{-(\phi(x)+i\mu)(y+jd)} = \gamma(s,y) T^2$, and observe average $\gamma \ge \beta$.

nodes.name: General bilinear lemma giving quadratic polynomial
nodes.statement: For real $f_1, f_2, f_3$ with $\sum_{i,j} f_1(i)f_2(j)f_3(i+j)\omega^{-(ai + bj - 2cij)} \ge cT^2$, define Fourier transforms $g_1, g_2, g_3$; Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\|g_1\|_\infty \|g_2\|_2 \|g_3\|_2 \ge cT^2 N$, hence $\exists$ quadratic $\psi$ with $|\sum_i f_1(i)\omega^{-\psi(i)}| \ge cT/\sqrt{2}$.

nodes.name: Average over $s$ to conclude
nodes.statement: Apply the bilinear lemma to $f_1, f_2, f_3$ derived from $f$ and average over $s$, choosing $\psi_s$ to obtain the conclusion.

nodes.name: Weyl-type Quadratic Equidistribution Estimate
nodes.statement: Let $N$ be sufficiently large and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_N$. For any $t \le N$ there exists $p \le t$ such that $|p^2 a| \le C t^{-1/8} N$, where $C$ is an absolute constant.
conclusions: There exists $p \le t$ with $|p^2 a| \le C t^{-1/8} N$.
nodes.origin_citation: Weyl 1913 (with bounds derived from Weyl's inequality)

nodes.name: Dirichlet-type Partition for Linear Functions
nodes.statement: Let $\phi : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ be linear ($\phi(x) = ax + b$) and $r, s \le N$. For some $m \le (2rN/s)^{1/2}$, $\{0, 1, \ldots, r-1\}$ can be partitioned into APs $P_1, \ldots, P_m$ such that $\mathrm{diam}(\phi(P_j)) \le s$ for every $j$, with sizes differing by at most 1.
conclusions: Partition into $m \le (2rN/s)^{1/2}$ APs $P_1, \ldots, P_m$ with $\mathrm{diam}(\phi(P_j)) \le s$ and sizes differing by $\le 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 17
nodes.statement: Pigeonhole among $\phi(0), \ldots, \phi(t)$ to find $u \le t$ with $|\phi(u) - \phi(0)| \le N/t$. Split $\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$ into $u$ congruence classes mod $u$ and partition each into APs of length $\le st/N$.

nodes.name: Partition for Quadratic Polynomial Diameter Control
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant $C$ such that for any quadratic polynomial $\psi : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ and $r \in \mathbb{N}$, $\{0, 1, \ldots, r-1\}$ can be partitioned into APs $P_1, \ldots, P_m$ with $m \le C r^{1-1/128}$ and $\mathrm{diam}(\psi(P_j)) \le C r^{-1/128} N$, sizes differing by at most 1.
conclusions: Partition into APs $P_1, \ldots, P_m$ with $m \le C r^{1-1/128}$ and $\mathrm{diam}(\psi(P_j)) \le C r^{-1/128} N$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 18
nodes.statement: Use Theorem 16 to find $p \le r^{1/2}$ with $|ap^2| \le C_1 r^{-1/8} N$, expand $\psi(x+sp) = s^2(ap^2) + \theta(x,p)$ with bilinear $\theta$; partition into APs $Q_j$ of step $p$ then refine each via Lemma 17 with linear $\phi_j$ on the residual.

nodes.name: From Quadratic Bias to Linear Sums
nodes.statement: Let $\psi : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ be a quadratic polynomial and $r \le N$. There exists $m \le C r^{1-1/128}$ and a partition $\{0,1,\ldots,r-1\} = P_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup P_m$ into APs of nearly equal size such that for any $f : \mathbb{Z}_N \to \mathbb{D}$ with $|\sum_{x=0}^{r-1} f(x) \omega^{-\psi(x)}| \ge \alpha r$, $\sum_{j=1}^m |\sum_{x \in P_j} f(x)| \ge \alpha r / 2$.
conclusions: $\sum_{j=1}^m |\sum_{x\in P_j} f(x)| \ge \alpha r / 2$

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 19
nodes.statement: Apply Proposition 18 to get $\mathrm{diam}(\psi(P_j)) \le \alpha N / (4\pi)$; on each $P_j$ replace $\omega^{-\psi(x)}$ by $\omega^{-\psi(x_j)}$ at cost $\alpha/2$; triangle inequality gives the conclusion.

nodes.name: Main Theorem (4-AP Density Increment)
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, if $A \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ has $|A| = \delta N$ and $N \ge \exp\exp\exp((1/\delta)^C)$, then $A$ contains an arithmetic progression of length four.
conclusions: $A$ contains a 4-term arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 20
nodes.statement: Density-increment argument: if no 4-AP, $A$ fails to be quadratically uniform (Cor 8); chain Lemmas 2/Prop 9/Cor 14/Prop 15/Cor 19 to find an AP $P_{sj}$ with $|A \cap P_{sj}| \ge (\delta + c_2 \beta)|P_{sj}|$; iterate; bound iterations by $\exp((1/\delta)^K)$ to derive the triple-exponential lower bound on $N$.

nodes.name: Contradiction setup: assume no 4-AP
nodes.statement: Suppose $A$ has no 4-AP. Corollary 8 implies $A$ is not quadratically $2^{-208}\delta^{112}$-uniform. Set $\alpha = 2^{-208}\delta^{112}$.

nodes.name: Extract $B, \phi$ via Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Lemma 2(ii→iii) gives $B \subset \mathbb{Z}_N$ with $|B| \ge \alpha N / 2$ and $\phi : B \to \mathbb{Z}_N$ with $|\Delta(f;k)^\sim(\phi(k))| \ge (\alpha/2)^{1/2} N$ for all $k \in B$.

nodes.name: Many additive quadruples via Proposition 9
nodes.statement: Sum gives $\sum_{k\in B}|\Delta(f;k)^\sim(\phi(k))|^2 \ge (\alpha/2)^2 N^3$, so by Proposition 9, $\phi$ has $\ge (\alpha/2)^8 N^3$ additive quadruples.

nodes.name: Linear structure via Corollary 14, then quadratic bias via Proposition 15
nodes.statement: Corollary 14 gives a long AP $P$ with $T \ge N^\gamma$ where $\phi$ matches a linear function; Proposition 15 yields quadratic polynomials $\psi_s$ with $\sum_s |\sum_{z\in P+s} f(z)\omega^{-\psi_s(z)}| \ge \beta N T / \sqrt{2}$.

nodes.name: Partition via Corollary 19 and find density-increment AP
nodes.statement: Apply Corollary 19 to partition $P + s$ into $P_{sj}$; pass to genuine APs (Lemma 17) and use $\sum f = 0$ to show $\exists s, j$ with $|A \cap P_{sj}| \ge (\delta + c_2 \beta)|P_{sj}|$.

nodes.name: Iterate density increment and bound iterations
nodes.statement: Repeat on $A \cap P_{sj}$. Density goes up by factor $\ge 1 + c_2 \beta$; can be repeated $\le \exp((1/\delta)^K)$ times. Each step replaces $N$ with $N^{\delta^K}$. Setting $r = \exp((1/\delta)^K)$ and $\theta = \delta^K$, we need $N^{\theta^r} \ge 200\delta^{-3}$, giving the triple-exponential bound.

nodes.name: Coloring Corollary for 4-APs
nodes.statement: There is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that if $\{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$ is coloured with at most $(\log\log\log N)^c$ colours, then there is a monochromatic arithmetic progression of length four.
assumptions: $\{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$ is coloured with $\le (\log\log\log N)^c$ colours
conclusions: There is a monochromatic 4-term arithmetic progression.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 21
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 20 to the largest colour class, whose density is $\ge 1/(\log\log\log N)^c \ge (\log\log\log N)^{-c}$ matching the bound.
